plan: Genesis 7:1-24; Genesis 8:1-22; Genesis 9:1-17, 18–10:1; Genesis 10:2-5; 1 Chronicles 1:5-7; Genesis 10:6-20; 1 Chronicles 1:8-16; Genesis 10:21-30; 1 Chronicles 1:17-23; Genesis 10:31-32

readings.title: The Great Deluge
readings.subtitle: The Fountains of the Deep Burst Open
readings.text: [Genesis 7:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Noaḥ, <dq>“Come into the ark, you and all your household, because <dn>I</dn> have seen that <dn>את</dn> you are righteous before <dn>Me</dn> in this generation.</dq> [2] <dq>“Of every clean beast take with you seven pairs, a male and his female; and of the beast that is not clean two, a male and his female;</dq> [3] <dq>“and of birds of the heavens seven pairs, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the face of all the earth.</dq> [4] <dq>“For after seven more days <dn>I</dn> am sending rain on the earth, forty days and forty nights, and <dn>I</dn> shall wipe from the face of the earth all that stands that <dn>I</dn> have created.”</dq> [5] And Noaḥ did according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded him. [6] Now Noaḥ was six hundred years old when the floodwaters were on the earth. [7] And Noaḥ and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him went into the ark because of the waters of the flood. [8] Of clean beasts and of beasts that are not clean, and of birds, and of all that creep on the earth, [9] two by two they went into the ark to Noaḥ, male and female, as <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded Noaḥ. [10] And it came to be after seven days that the waters of the flood were on the earth. [11] In the six hundredth year of the life of Noaḥ, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of the heavens were opened. [12] And the rain was on the earth forty days and forty nights. [13] On that very same day Noaḥ and Shĕm and Ḥam and Yepheth, the sons of Noaḥ, and Noaḥ’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered the ark, [14] they and every beast after its kind, and all cattle after their kind, and every creeping creature that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort. [15] And they went into the ark to Noaḥ, two by two, of all flesh in which is the breath of life. [16] And those going in, male and female of all flesh, went in as <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded him; and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shut him in. [17] And the flood was on the earth forty days, and the waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the earth. [18] And the waters were mighty and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark moved about on the surface of the waters. [19] And the waters were exceedingly mighty on the earth, and all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered. [20] The waters prevailed fifteen cubits upward, and the mountains were covered. [21] And all flesh died that moved on the earth: birds and cattle and beasts and every creeping creature that creeps on the earth, and every man. [22] All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, all that was on the dry land, died. [23] So <dn>He</dn> wiped off all that stood, which were on the face of the ground – both man and beast, creeping creature and bird of the heavens. And they were wiped off from the earth. And only Noaḥ was left, and those with him in the ark. [24] And the waters were mighty on the earth, one hundred and fifty days.

readings.title: The Waters Recede
readings.subtitle: A Wind Passes Over the Earth
readings.text: [Genesis 8:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> remembered Noaḥ, and every living being, and all the cattle that were with him in the ark. And <dn>Elohim</dn> made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided. [2] And the fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were stopped, and the rain from the heavens was withheld. [3] And the waters receded steadily from the earth, and at the end of the hundred and fifty days the waters diminished. [4] And in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark rested on the mountains of Ararat. [5] And the waters decreased steadily until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains became visible. [6] And it came to be, at the end of forty days, that Noaḥ opened the window of the ark which he had made, [7] and he sent out a raven, which kept going out and turning back until the waters had dried up from the earth. [8] Then he sent out a dove from him, to see if the waters had receded from the face of the ground. [9] But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned into the ark to him, for the waters were on the face of all the earth. So he put out his hand and took her, and drew her into the ark to himself. [10] And he waited yet another seven days, and again he sent the dove out from the ark. [11] And the dove came to him in the evening, and see, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in her mouth. And Noaḥ knew that the waters had receded from the earth. [12] And he waited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove, which did not return to him again. [13] And it came to be in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, that the waters were dried up from the earth. And Noaḥ removed the covering of the ark and looked, and see, the surface of the ground was dry. [14] And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry. [15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to Noaḥ, saying, [16] <dq>“Go out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.</dq> [17] <dq>“Bring out with you every living being of all flesh that is with you: birds and cattle and every creeping creature that creeps on the earth, so that they abound on the earth, and be fruitful and increase on the earth.”</dq> [18] So Noaḥ went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him. [19] Every beast, every creeping creature, and every bird, whatever creeps on the earth, according to their kinds, went out of the ark. [20] And Noaḥ built an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and took of every clean beast and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smelled a soothing fragrance, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said in <dn>His</dn> heart, <dq>“Never again shall <dn>I</dn> curse the ground for man’s sake, although the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth, and never again smite all living creatures, as <dn>I</dn> have done.</dq> [22] <dq>“As long as the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and winter and summer, and day and night shall not cease.”</dq>

readings.title: The Rainbow Covenant
readings.subtitle: Reminder of The Just Standards
readings.text: [Genesis 9:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> blessed Noaḥ and his sons, and said to them, <dq>“Be fruitful and increase, and fill the earth.</dq> [2] <dq>“And the fear of you and the dread of you is on every beast of the earth, on every bird of the heavens, on all that moves on the earth, and on all the fish of the sea – into your hand they have been given.</dq> [3] <dq>“Every moving creature that lives is food for you. <dn>I</dn> have given you all, as <dn>I</dn> gave the green plants.</dq> [4] <dq>“But do not eat flesh with its life, its blood.</dq> [5] <dq>“And indeed, your blood of your lives <dn>I</dn> require. From the hand of every beast <dn>I</dn> require it, and from the hand of man. From the hand of every man’s brother <dn>I</dn> require the life of man.</dq> [6] <dq>“Whoever sheds man’s blood, by man his blood is shed. For in the image of <dn>Elohim</dn> has <dn>He</dn> made man.</dq> [7] <dq>“As for you, be fruitful and increase, bring forth swarms in the earth, and increase in it.”</dq> [8] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to Noaḥ and to his sons with him, saying, [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn>, see, <dn>I</dn> establish <dn>My</dn> covenant with you and with your seed after you,</dq> [10] <dq>“and with every living being that is with you: of the birds, the cattle, and every beast of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ark, every beast of the earth.</dq> [11] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>My</dn> covenant with you, and never again is all flesh cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again is there a flood to destroy the earth.”</dq> [12] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“This is the sign of the covenant which <dn>I</dn> make between <dn>Me</dn> and you, and every living being that is with you, for all generations:</dq> [13] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> rainbow in the cloud, and it shall be for the sign of the covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and the earth.</dq> [14] <dq>“And it shall be, when <dn>I</dn> bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow shall be seen in the cloud;</dq> [15] <dq>“and <dn>I</dn> shall remember <dn>My</dn> covenant which is between <dn>Me</dn> and you and every living being of all flesh, and the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.</dq> [16] <dq>“And the rainbow shall be in the cloud, and <dn>I</dn> shall see it, to remember the everlasting covenant between <dn>Elohim</dn> and every living being of all flesh that is on the earth.”</dq> [17] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Noaḥ, <dq>“This is the sign of the covenant which <dn>I</dn> have established between <dn>Me</dn> and all flesh that is on the earth.”</dq>

readings.title: Kenaʽan Uncovers the 'Nakedness' of Noaḥ (euphemism for his wife)
readings.subtitle: Prophecies Regarding the Nations
readings.text: [Genesis 9:18] And the sons of Noaḥ who went out of the ark were Shĕm, Ḥam, and Yepheth. And Ḥam was the father of Kenaʽan. [19] These three were the sons of Noaḥ, and from these the whole earth was populated. [20] And Noaḥ, a man of the soil, began and planted a vineyard. [21] And he drank of the wine and was drunk, and became uncovered in his tent. [22] And Ḥam, the father of Kenaʽan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside. [23] And Shĕm and Yepheth took a garment, laid it on both their shoulders, and went backward and covered the nakedness of their father. And their faces were turned away, and they did not see their father’s nakedness. [24] And Noaḥ awoke from his wine, and he knew what his younger son had done to him, [25] and he said, “Cursed is Kenaʽan, let him be a servant of servants to his brothers.” [26] And he said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Shĕm, and let Kenaʽan be his servant. [27] “Let <dn>Elohim</dn> enlarge Yepheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shĕm. And let Kenaʽan be his servant.” [28] And Noaḥ lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years. [29] So all the days of Noaḥ were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died. [Genesis 10:1] And this is the genealogy of the sons of Noaḥ: Shĕm, Ḥam, and Yepheth. And sons were born to them after the flood.

readings.title: The Sons of Yepheth
readings.subtitle: The Expansion to the Coastlands
readings.text: [Genesis 10:2] The sons of Yepheth: Gomer, and Maḡoḡ, and Maḏai, and Yavan, and Tuḇal, and Mesheḵ, and Tiras. [3] And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Toḡarmah. [4] And the sons of Yavan: Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Doḏanim. [5] From these the coastland peoples of the gentiles were separated into their lands, everyone according to his language, according to their families, into their nations. [1 Chronicles 1:5] The sons of Yepheth: Gomer, and Maḡoḡ, and Maḏai, and Yavan, and Tuḇal, and Mesheḵ, and Tiras. [6] And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Toḡarmah. [7] And the sons of Yavan: Elishah, and Tarshishah, Kittim, and Roḏanim.

readings.title: The Sons of Ḥam
readings.subtitle: Nimrod and the Mighty Ones
readings.text: [Genesis 10:6] And the sons of Ḥam: Kush, and Mitsrayim, and Put, and Kenaʽan. [7] And the sons of Kush: Seḇa, and Ḥavilah, and Saḇtah, and Raʽmah, and Saḇteḵa. And the sons of Raʽmah: Sheḇa and Deḏan. [8] And Kush brought forth Nimroḏ, he began to be a mighty one on the earth. [9] He was a mighty hunter before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, therefore it is said, “Like Nimroḏ the mighty hunter before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [10] And the beginning of his reign was Baḇel, and Ereḵ, and Akkaḏ, and Kalneh, in the land of Shinʽar. [11] From that land he went to Ashshur and built Ninevĕh, and Reḥoḇoth Ir, and Kalaḥ, [12] and Resen between Ninevĕh and Kalaḥ, that is the great city. [13] And Mitsrayim brought forth Luḏim, and Anamim, and Lehaḇim, and Naphtuḥim, [14] and Pathrusim, and Kasluḥim, from whom came the Philistines and Kaphtorim. [15] And Kenaʽan brought forth Siḏon his first-born, and Ḥĕth, [16] and the Yeḇusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite, [17] and the Ḥivite, and the Arqite, and the Sinite, [18] and the Arvaḏite, and the Tsemarite, and the Ḥamathite. And afterward the families of the Kenaʽanites were spread abroad. [19] And the border of the Kenaʽanites was from Siḏon as you go toward Gerar, as far as Azzah; as you go toward Seḏom and Amorah and Aḏmah and Tseḇoyim, as far as Lasha. [20] These were the sons of Ḥam, according to their families, according to their languages, in their lands and in their nations. [1 Chronicles 1:8] The sons of Ḥam: Kush, and Mitsrayim, Put, and Kenaʽan. [9] And the sons of Kush: Seḇa, and Ḥavilah, and Saḇta, and Raʽma, and Saḇteḵa. And the sons of Raʽma: Sheḇa and Deḏan. [10] And Kush brought forth Nimroḏ. He began to be a mighty one on the earth. [11] And Mitsrayim brought forth Luḏim, and Anamim, and Lehaḇim, and Naphtuḥim, [12] and Pathrusim, and Kasluḥim, from whom came the Philistines and Kaphtorim. [13] And Kenaʽan brought forth Siḏon his first-born, and Ḥĕth, [14] and the Yeḇusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite, [15] and the Ḥivite, and the Arqite, and the Sinite, [16] and the Arvaḏite, and the Tsemarite, and the Ḥamathite.

readings.title: The Sons of Shĕm
readings.subtitle: The Line of the Messiah
readings.text: [Genesis 10:21] And also to Shĕm, the father of all the children of Ěḇer, the brother of Yepheth the elder, children were born. [22] The sons of Shĕm: Ělam, and Ashshur, and Arpaḵshaḏ, and Luḏ, and Aram. [23] And the sons of Aram: Uts, and Ḥul, and Gether, and Mash. [24] And Arpaḵshaḏ brought forth Shelaḥ, and Shelaḥ brought forth Ěḇer. [25] And to Ěḇer were born two sons: the name of one was Peleḡ, for in his days the earth was divided; and his brother’s name was Yoqtan. [26] And Yoqtan brought forth Almoḏaḏ, and Sheleph, and Ḥatsarmaveth, and Yeraḥ, [27] and Haḏoram, and Uzal, and Diqlah, [28] and Oḇal, and Aḇima’ĕl, and Sheḇa, [29] and Ophir, and Ḥavilah, and Yoḇab. All these were the sons of Yoqtan. [30] And their dwelling place was from Mĕsha as you go toward Sephar, a mountain of the east. [1 Chronicles 1:17] The sons of Shĕm: Ělam, and Ashshur, and Arpaḵshaḏ, and Luḏ, and Aram, and Uts, and Ḥul, and Gether, and Mesheḵ. [18] And Arpaḵshaḏ brought forth Shelaḥ, and Shelaḥ brought forth Ěḇer. [19] And to Ěḇer were born two sons: the name of one was Peleḡ, for in his days the earth was divided; and his brother’s name was Yoqtan. [20] And Yoqtan brought forth Almoḏaḏ, and Sheleph, and Ḥatsarmaveth, and Yeraḥ, [21] and Haḏoram, and Uzal, and Diqlah, [22] and Ěḇal, and Aḇima’ĕl, and Sheḇa, [23] and Ophir, and Ḥavilah, and Yoḇab. All these were the sons of Yoqtan. [Genesis 10:31] These were the sons of Shĕm, according to their families, according to their languages, in their lands, according to their nations. [32] These were the families of the sons of Noaḥ, according to their generations, in their nations. And from these the nations were divided on the earth after the flood. <img:seventy_nations.PNG>
